questions.question: An ambulance location model sets $y_j=1$ if a station is built in town $j$ (else 0), lets $N_i=\{j\colon t_{ij}\le18\}$ be the towns within 18 minutes of town $i$ ($t_{ij}$ = travel time), and minimizes $\sum_jy_j$ subject to $\sum_{j\in N_i}y_j\ge1$ for every town $i$. Which requirement is NOT guaranteed by this model?
options: That no station serves more towns than it can handle
That every town has a station within 18 minutes
That the number of stations built is as small as possible
That each station decision is either yes or no

questions.question: An ambulance location model sets $y_j=1$ if a station is built in town $j$ (else 0), lets $N_i=\{j\colon t_{ij}\le18\}$ be the towns within 18 minutes of town $i$ ($t_{ij}$ = travel time), and minimizes $\sum_jy_j$ subject to $\sum_{j\in N_i}y_j\ge1$ for every town $i$. A modeller relaxes $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ to $0\le y_j\le1$. What can go wrong?
options: The model becomes infeasible, since fractions cannot cover
Nothing, since the minimum count is a whole number anyway
Fractions such as $y_1=y_2=0.5$ can cover a town on paper
The objective may now exceed the true minimum station count

questions.question: Travel times (minutes) from town 2 to towns 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 are 12, 0, 18, 25 and 19. With coverage meaning travel time at most 18 minutes, which set is $N_2$, the towns from which a station would cover town 2?
In an ambulance location model with binary $y_j$ (station in town $j$), the towns within 18 minutes of town 4 are towns 2, 4 and 5. Which constraint correctly requires coverage of town 4?

Six towns have coverage sets $N_1=\{1,3,4,6\}$, $N_2=\{2,3\}$, $N_3=\{1,2,3\}$, $N_4=\{1,4,5\}$, $N_5=\{4,5,6\}$, $N_6=\{1,5,6\}$ ($N_i$: towns whose station would cover town $i$). Do stations in towns 1 and 5 cover every town?
options: No, since town 2 is not covered
Yes, as they reach 7 towns in total
No, since town 3 is not covered
Yes, as town 1 covers four towns

questions.question: In an ambulance location model with binary $y_j$ (station in town $j$), town 3 is within 18 minutes of towns 2, 3 and 4. Town 3 is large and must be within 18 minutes of at least two stations. Which constraint models this?

In an ambulance location model with binary $y_j$ and coverage constraints $\sum_{j\in N_i}y_j\ge1$, town 5 is more than 18 minutes from every other town, so $N_5=\{5\}$. What follows for every feasible solution?
options: $y_5\le1$ only

questions.question: A model chooses binary $y_j$ (station in town $j$) to minimize the number of stations so that each town has a station within a time threshold. The threshold is tightened from 18 to 15 minutes, travel times unchanged. What happens to the minimum number of stations?
options: It stays the same or increases
It stays the same or decreases
It always increases by at least one
It always stays exactly the same

questions.question: A station-location model minimizes $\sum_jy_j$ over binary $y_j$ (station in town $j$) subject to one constraint $\sum_{j\in N_i}y_j\ge1$ per town $i$, where $N_i$ lists the towns within 18 minutes of town $i$. Why is it always feasible, whatever the travel times?
options: One station always covers all towns within 18 minutes
Binary variables make every covering model feasible
Minimizing $\sum_jy_j$ makes the all-zero plan feasible
Building in every town covers all, since each $i\in N_i$

questions.question: In a station-location model with binary $y_j$, town $i$ needs $\sum_{j\in N_i}y_j\ge1$, where $N_i$ is the set of towns whose station covers town $i$. Suppose $N_1=\{1,2\}$ and $N_2=\{1,2,3\}$. What can be said about the constraints of towns 1 and 2?
options: Town 1's constraint is redundant, since $N_1$ is the smaller set
Both are needed, since they belong to different towns
Town 2's constraint can be dropped, as town 1's implies it
A station must be built in town 2, which lies in both sets

questions.question: Six towns on a line have $N_1=\{1,2\}$, $N_2=\{1,2,3\}$, $N_3=\{2,3,4\}$, $N_4=\{3,4,5\}$, $N_5=\{4,5,6\}$, $N_6=\{5,6\}$. Building costs are 10, 30, 12, 12, 30, 10 in towns 1 to 6. Covering every town, what is the minimum total building cost?

Four towns have travel times $t_{12}=10$, $t_{13}=18$, $t_{14}=16$, $t_{23}=25$, $t_{24}=20$, $t_{34}=12$ minutes (symmetric). With an 18-minute threshold one station in town 1 covers all towns. How many stations are needed if the threshold becomes 15 minutes?

Six towns must each have an ambulance station within 18 minutes (a town covers itself), using as few stations as possible; $z$ is that minimum number. Town 4 is within 18 minutes of every town except town 6. What is known about $z$?
options: $z=2$ exactly, since town 4 misses town 6
$z\le2$, and $z=2$ only if town 6 is isolated
$z=1$, since town 4 covers five of six towns
$z\le2$, and $z=1$ needs a town reaching all

questions.question: Three towns each lie within 18 minutes of exactly one other: $N_1=\{1,2\}$, $N_2=\{2,3\}$, $N_3=\{3,1\}$ ($N_i$: sites whose station covers town $i$). A modeller writes the coverage constraints as $\sum_{j\in N_i}y_j=1$ with binary $y_j$. What happens?
options: The optimum is one station, since each town needs exactly one
The optimum is $y_1=y_2=y_3=0.5$, a fractional covering plan
No binary solution exists, though two stations cover all towns
Nothing changes, as $=1$ and $\ge1$ agree for binary variables

questions.question: Six towns have $N_1=\{1,3,4,6\}$, $N_2=\{2,3\}$, $N_3=\{1,2,3\}$, $N_4=\{1,4,5\}$, $N_5=\{4,5,6\}$, $N_6=\{1,5,6\}$. A planner first builds where the most towns are covered (town 1), then repeats for the rest. How many stations does the true minimum need?

Seven towns on a line each lie within 18 minutes only of themselves and their direct neighbours, e.g. $N_1=\{1,2\}$, $N_4=\{3,4,5\}$, $N_7=\{6,7\}$. Stations in towns 2, 5 and 7 cover all towns. Which observation proves that no plan with two stations exists?
options: Towns 1, 4 and 7 have pairwise disjoint sets $N_i$
Towns 1, 3 and 5 are pairwise more than 18 minutes apart
Towns 2, 4 and 6 each cover three towns at once
The line of seven towns has two end towns, 1 and 7
